transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because lately, any time I have to get near a scaffold, a roof edge, or an upper platform, I get this strong feeling like I’m going to go over. Even when I can see the guardrails are there and I know it’s supposed to be safe, my head just tells me I’m about to fall.
Does this feeling happen only when you’re near high places?

Yes, it’s really just when I’m up near high places or right at the edge of something—like scaffolds, roof edges, upper platforms. That’s when my head starts telling me I’m about to go over, even if I can see the rails are there and I know it should be safe.
When you’re near a high place and this happens, do you get a sudden panic attack?

It’s sudden, yeah. The second I step onto temporary stairs or even start walking toward an open upper floor, my chest tightens up, my hands get sweaty, and it feels like my legs might just lock before I can take another step.
Do you avoid high places because of this fear?

Yes. I’ve been avoiding them as much as I can. I hand off height inspections to my foremen now, and I try to move meetings down to ground level. If I absolutely have to go up, I make sure someone stays right beside me, and I just rush through it scared the whole time.
Have you ever had one of these panic episodes when you were not near a high place?
No, I don’t think so. I can’t remember it happening out of nowhere or when I’m just at ground level. It’s tied to being up high or close to an edge.
